$source_revision._note: Initial seed for issue #98. The proton-radius puzzle is the load-bearing disagreement-representation demonstrator.

values._note: Pohl et al. 2010 Nature 466, 213. The measurement that triggered the proton-radius puzzle.
Bernauer et al. 2010 A1 Collaboration Mainz electron-proton elastic scattering measurement.
CODATA-2018 recommended value, weighted average of pre-muonic-puzzle hydrogen-spectroscopy + electron-scattering data.
Fleurbaey et al. 2018 Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 183001. H 1S-3S two-photon spectroscopy yields a value consistent with muonic H, contradicting the prior CODATA average.
Xiong et al. (PRad Collaboration) 2019 Nature 575, 147. Low-Q^2 electron scattering at JLab; agrees with muonic H within uncertainty.

charge_radius._note: Proton-radius puzzle: muonic H spectroscopy + recent low-Q^2 e-scattering + H 1S-3S yield rp ~ 0.84 fm; older A1 Mainz e-scattering + CODATA-2018 pre-puzzle yield rp ~ 0.88 fm. Disagreement at the ~5 sigma level is itself physics — the umbrella's disagreement-representation rule (#92 §5) surfaces all values rather than averaging them away.

magnetic_moment._note: Proton magnetic moment in units of nuclear magnetons mu_N = e*hbar/(2*m_p*c).

n.description: Neutron — Z=0, A=1; mean charge radius (rms) deduced from electron-scattering form factor

charge_radius._note: Neutron is electrically neutral overall; its mean-square charge radius <r^2>_n is -0.1161(22) fm^2. Listed here as null because a single 'radius' value is not a clean observable; see <r^2>_n below.

mean_square_charge_radius._note: <r^2>_n = -0.1161(22) fm^2. The negative sign reflects that the negative-charge cloud (one d quark) extends farther on average than the positive (two u quarks).

d.description: Deuteron — bound state of one proton + one neutron, Z=1, A=2

values._note: Pohl et al. 2016 Science 353, 669. Analogous to proton-radius puzzle; muonic D yields r_d ~ 2.126 fm.
CODATA-2018 recommended value, derived from H/D isotope-shift spectroscopy.

charge_radius._note: Deuteron-radius puzzle analogue to proton-radius puzzle. Tension at the ~3 sigma level depending on which measurements are included.
